day.reading: neutral drift is no retreat; bottlenecks or deme replacement at best halve the fixation time ("done the math")
day.holds: the premise holds at N_e of 33,000 (3.83 My) or 198,000 (19.8 My) against 1-2 My; the halving is unreleased here (no derivation held), so it is neither confirmed nor refuted

critic.reading: Gemini's concessions are an LLM output; the lifespan premise and what counts as one lineage are open
critic.holds: at the textbook N_e = 1e4, 4 N_e = 1.0 My, inside the 1-2 My range, so the premise depends on N_e; Day's own Hard Limits paper calls 'nothing finishes in the species lifetime' 'simply wrong as a claim about throughput' (B2d), and narrows to the fill state (M-202)

notes: Model-choice: no single number settles it. The halving at 'the optimal population level' has no held derivation (mailvox@L14 'I've done the math on that as well'); it is recorded as unreleased, not asserted. The relayed Gemini sentence is rule U. Whether a species boundary ends a lineage for fixation counting (daughter species inherit the 'unresolved pipeline', mailvox@L8) is not settled by any held derivation. Steady-state throughput (mu per site) versus fill state is M-111/M-201 and M-202.
